rows.name: A1_ladder_resid_fade_1d
rows.mechanism: Every Treasury wrapper is a claim on one segment of the SAME published constant-maturity curve, and the US Treasury publishes that curve every business day for free.  Strip out each wrapper's move that its OWN published key rate explains and what remains is the wrapper dislocating from the published claim.  Index funds are mandate-locked to their maturity bucket and cannot move to the cheap segment; only authorised participants can, and only at T+1 with a real Treasury basket to source, so the dislocation is closed with a lag.

rows.name: C1_begap_TIP_IEF_5d
rows.mechanism: FRED publishes the 5y and 10y breakeven inflation rate every business day.  A TIPS wrapper held against a duration-matched NOMINAL wrapper is a tradable long-breakeven book, so its return must track the PUBLISHED breakeven.  The gap between the two is a tradable claim priced against a third-party published anchor -- structurally the same object as a closed-end fund's discount to NAV.  TIPS are the least liquid Treasury instrument and the first leg a levered relative-value book liquidates, so the gap opens on forced flow, not on information.

rows.name: D1_rolldown_daily
rows.mechanism: The shape of the published curve IS the term premium.  Carry plus roll-down per unit duration is computable from the published curve alone -- no estimation, no fitting -- and it is the structural reason one maturity bucket out-earns another.  Index funds are mandate-locked to their bucket and cannot migrate to the richest point on the curve, so the compensation survives inside the complex.

rows.name: F1_flygap_10d
rows.mechanism: The published curve pins CURVATURE as well as level and slope: the 2s-7s-30s butterfly is a number the Treasury publishes daily.  A duration-weighted belly-versus-wings ETF book is the tradable expression of exactly that number, so the gap between the two is a published-anchor dislocation.  Mortgage servicers and GSEs are structurally short convexity and must hedge at the wings on a schedule set by lock periods, which is what opens the gap.

rows.name: E1_decoy_BIL_vs_publishedbill
rows.mechanism: NEGATIVE CONTROL.  BIL has essentially no duration, so its return IS the published 3-month bill yield over 252 and nothing else.  Any 'residual' here is pure tick bounce.  If this scores, a high gross Sharpe in this complex means bounce, not edge.

rows.name: E2_decoy_TLH_follows_TLT
rows.mechanism: DECOY / positive control for the lag test.  TLH is the thinnest nominal Treasury wrapper (51k shares/day) and should LAG TLT's print.  A large lag-0 diagnostic here with nothing at lag 1 is the signature of quote staleness.
